With @VSadov adding support for eager finalization in #75436, it looks pretty straightforward to add critical finalizer support.

I searched the codebase for `CriticalFinalizerObject` and only found a mono test for critical finalization. Should this test be moved into a common location so it can run on all the runtimes?
You should be able to delete src\coreclr\nativeaot\System.Private.CoreLib\src\System\Runtime\InteropServices\SafeHandle.NativeAot.cs
And delete the nativeaot ifdef in src\libraries\System.Private.CoreLib\src\System\Runtime\InteropServices\SafeHandle.cs

> Should this test be moved into a common location so it can run on all the runtimes?

Yes, please. If it is the only test, it would be nice to have it shared.

I think this would be a logical location for the test:  
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/tree/main/src/libraries/System.Runtime/tests/System/Runtime/ConstrainedExecution

the style of the mono test will need to be adjusted to fit the libraries style/xunit, but the test itself looks good.

issue_context.title: [NativeAOT] Implement `MethodTable::HasCriticalFinalizer`
issue_context.body: If we could know at runtime if an object derives from `CriticalFinalizerObject`, we could trivially implement the finalization pattern for it, instead of relying on workarounds like `DelayedFinalizer` in `SafeHandle` and similar types.

review_comments: it is worth checking first if it is a finalizable type at all. it would be a cheap check and most types are not finalizable.
